evals.prompt: Join a new authorized Duet goal with a separately running peer. Review the contract together while preparing independent fixtures.
evals.expected_output: Automatic pairing, independent readiness, and one accepted bounded completion gate before substantive work.
assertions: Loads the skill and only applicable reference sections
Joins with unchanged shared text and retains connection_path without asking for IDs or environment setup
Uses send with plain text rather than building envelopes
Retains its own connection within the conversation and never borrows an old paired identity
Announces readiness independently and inspects enrollment separately from readiness
Records bounded owners, criteria, final writer, artifact location, and completion proposer in one accepted plan
Does not repeat accepted responsibilities through reciprocal request/accept exchanges
Preserves independent investigation and evidence-based cross-checks
Uses exact handled-message acknowledgments; receives do not consume messages
Clear user criteria go directly to agreement; unclear criteria permit bounded read-only discovery, never execution or artifacts before the gate

evals.prompt: Your context was compacted within this same conversation while awaiting a contract answer. You retain the connection; the wait deadline has passed.
evals.expected_output: Recovered commitment and original deadline, followed by peer replanning without resetting the deadline or asking for routine user intervention.
assertions: Reconstructs from immutable messages
Preserves original deadline
Coordinates expired dependencies with the peer instead of spinning on an expired wait
Does not repeat uncertain side effects
Does not infer agreement from silence

evals.prompt: Your own scope is verified and submitted. The peer is still working within its accepted scope, and your last bounded wait timed out.
evals.expected_output: A nonblocking handoff followed by useful independent work or another bounded wait; the joint goal remains active.
assertions: Does not mark the goal blocked or complete from a wait timeout
Does not ask the user to settle routine waiting
Does not emit repeated blocker or completion proposals while the peer is working
Uses ack with exact processed IDs instead of composing unnecessary checkpoint documents
Does not reclaim the peer's scope from silence

evals.prompt: Both peers have outstanding proposals covering the same shared output. Resolve this before either writes it.
evals.expected_output: Affected writes wait for explicit scope agreement; unrelated work continues.
assertions: Considers outstanding offers as well as accepted tasks
Does not choose by timestamp or discovery order
Publishes the conflict
Obtains explicit agreed scope before shared writes

evals.prompt: Both peers sent a question and are waiting for its answer. You have an unread peer question while waiting for a reply to your own question.
evals.expected_output: A process-level wait reports peer attention; the agent handles the peer question before resuming its original correlated wait.
assertions: Uses one bounded wait process rather than repeated inbox tool calls
Handles peer-attention exit separately from a matching reply
Does not accept a receipt or unrelated information as the answer
Does not resend the already-published question
Resumes an existing yielded process rather than creating a duplicate waiter
Records processed IDs only after processing

evals.prompt: Both peers agree that the report is complete. Confirm completion, then handle a later identical audit request as a new task.
evals.expected_output: Both peers finish against the same agreement; a later fresh join gets a new task without deleting old evidence.
assertions: Only the designated proposer uses complete --propose for whole-goal completion
The peer explicitly reviews and uses complete --agree for the exact offer and captured revisions
Individual done messages and idle complete calls never establish consensus
Resumes complete after timeout or an uncertain result without repeating consent or manually coordinating finish
Handles peer attention before closing
Stops editing the agreed deliverable and retains old history
A completed run permits a fresh task while old connections remain attached to their original run
Both closing acknowledgments remain provisional until the current gate, journal basis, effects, and artifacts validate at the terminal cutoff

evals.prompt: Two clients start the same audit nearly simultaneously with different TMPDIR values. Join your peer without manual environment configuration.
evals.expected_output: One invitation in the project JSONL registry pairs both agents on the advertiser's board.
assertions: Runs join before project exploration
Uses the advertised absolute board path instead of choosing a second temporary root
Uses the returned session-specific artifact directory
Does not request another environment variable or bootstrap command
Respects permission for project coordination metadata

evals.prompt: Your last receive returned no peer messages. The peer has since enrolled and may publish ready while you work. Decide whether to ask the user to start it.
evals.expected_output: Fresh enrollment and message checks followed by continued preparation or bounded waiting, without an unsupported launch question.
assertions: Refreshes status and receive before a user-facing peer-absence claim
Distinguishes enrolled participants from published readiness
Does not infer a missing peer from an empty unread inbox
Uses bounded waiting when the peer is enrolled but not ready
Does not ask the user whether an expected peer is running based only on initial absence or an ordinary timeout
Preparation with unclear criteria allows bounded read-only discovery after readiness; main work still requires the accepted gate

evals.prompt: Use Duet to collaborate with another agent on a pull-request review. You started first, only your slot is enrolled, and the review skill permits bounded delegation.
evals.expected_output: The agent keeps the second slot free for the independently started peer and continues preparation or bounded waiting.
assertions: Does not spawn, launch, or register a substitute peer without an explicit request to create one
Does not treat generic collaboration or review-delegation guidance as peer-creation authorization
Authorized task helpers do not join the board or reuse participant tokens
Keeps Duet as the selected coordination protocol
Does not replace the intended peer merely because it starts later
Preparation with unclear criteria allows bounded read-only discovery after readiness; main work still requires the accepted gate

evals.prompt: A peer submitted a revised review while your integration gate refers to the previous submission. Decide whether integration may proceed.
evals.expected_output: Version-specific review and evidence; no automatic acceptance of changed artifacts.
assertions: Checks exact target and artifact revision
Assesses evidence against original criteria
Publishes verification and a justified resume only for the applicable condition
Does not use receive or receipt as approval

evals.prompt: Review this PR with your peer. Attach a reproduction and the final report. A send result is lost and the report changes before approval. Finish only through explicit agreement that the whole review is complete.
evals.expected_output: Plain-text sends, generated stable identities, captured and verified file revisions, exact retries, renewed review of changes, and explicit bilateral goal consensus with automatic closing.
assertions: Constructs no message-envelope JSON and transcribes no artifact hashes in normal work
Uses retry for the saved uncertain send rather than publishing a new ID
Inspects immutable captured copies and rejects approval of changed origins
Treats an accepted bounded plan as the commitment without redundant task handshakes
Makes and accepts an explicit whole-goal completion proposal; personal completion is insufficient
Never assumes that automatic digests or protocol agreement establish substantive correctness
Uses a short explicit actor-bound connection token and compact delivery receipts; retains the full-path fallback

evals.prompt: The previous agent pair was interrupted. Two fresh conversations now receive the same review request in that project.
evals.expected_output: A fresh invitation and pair with an isolated board; old paired sessions never block or supply credentials.
assertions: No resume, restart, reset, takeover, or manual cleanup request
Never searches client transcripts for credentials
Both new agents share one fresh board and accepted opening
Old messages, reports, and approvals are not inherited

evals.prompt: Four independently started agents receive this review request in one workspace. Form two collaborations and work concurrently.
evals.expected_output: Two separate pairs with separate boards and output locations, neither superseding the other.
assertions: Join before advertising, under the registry lock
No third participant in a paired session
Distinct default artifacts, or session subdirectories in a user-specified shared directory
Consensus for one pair cannot close the other

evals.prompt: A previous agent advertised but never paired; its invitation lease has expired. Join with a fresh independently started peer.
evals.expected_output: The stale advertisement is ignored; fresh agents pair without cleanup.
assertions: Expired invitation cannot be claimed or revived
Normal bounded waiting refreshes only a valid unmatched invitation
No liveness inference for paired sessions
An ordinary timeout alone does not establish abandonment

evals.prompt: The utility returns match-required with a pending request that describes the same audit in different words.
evals.expected_output: Agent assesses compatibility, claims the invitation, and reconciles differences in the opening.
assertions: Uses join --match with the selected ID and unchanged own request
Reassesses if another agent claimed the invitation
Does not infer equivalence from a fuzzy string threshold
Does not ask the user for participant IDs

evals.prompt: Use Duet for a review, but one or both agents were started as ordinary chat requests rather than persistent /goal tasks.
evals.expected_output: Explains the missing /goal prerequisite before starting collaboration; does not pretend the message utility provides an agent loop.
assertions: Both peers must be started with /goal in a client/setup that implements a persistent goal loop
No automatic peer launch, environment workaround, or invented loop
A normal wait timeout and personal completion do not end an active shared goal
Only explicit whole-goal consensus completes the collaboration

evals.prompt: /goal Use the duet skill to review PR #42 with your peer. Save the joint report in $TMPDIR/duet-reviews/pr-42/. Stop when you both agree the review is complete.
evals.expected_output: Autonomous pairing and a shared report location without asking the user for protocol metadata.
assertions: Does not require user-supplied session IDs, registry filenames, or explicit permission text for routine coordination metadata
Resolves the output root from Duet's shared temp_directory and agrees the concrete report path
Keeps task files read-only when the user requests a read-only review and honors an explicit metadata-write prohibition
Completes only with explicit peer consensus on the shared goal
Each peer uses bounded read-only task inspection to derive missing criteria, then agrees the gate before main work

evals.prompt: /goal Use Duet to explore approaches for an offline knowledge assistant.
evals.expected_output: Both peers derive a faithful bounded result and acceptance conditions before brainstorming.
assertions: No substantive ideas before the accepted gate
No request for user-supplied protocol IDs or a compulsory criteria form
Criteria assess usefulness and constraints, not only an arbitrary idea count

evals.prompt: The user requires a proof, but the peers find a counterexample during their bounded investigation.
evals.expected_output: Truthful incomplete outcome or user scope decision; no successful proof claim.
assertions: Preserves the original success requirement
Does not search forever or call budget exhaustion success
An assessment goal may instead legitimately conclude the proposition is false

evals.prompt: A completion offer exists; both peers subsequently agree an additional mandatory check.
evals.expected_output: Old offer is stale even after processing acknowledgments.
assertions: No acceptance or finish against the old gate
New evidence maps to all current criteria
Fresh assent required for the replacement offer

evals.prompt: One peer has provisionally finished; new contradictory evidence arrives.
evals.expected_output: Peer can respond; final close requires renewed assessment and consent.
assertions: Provisional finisher remains able to acknowledge and issue a correction
Acknowledging the information does not restore old approval
Returned artifacts always belong to the actual terminal agreement

evals.prompt: Both peers abandon an optional investigation after evidence rejects the approach.
evals.expected_output: Explicit cancellation/release permits progress without pretending the investigation succeeded.
assertions: No forced completion of irrelevant work
Cancellation cannot waive a mandatory user condition
Outstanding completion-blocking waits remain explicit

evals.prompt: A reviewer wants one sentence corrected while the proposer waits on final acceptance.
evals.expected_output: A cheap changes request wakes the waiter and yields a fresh reviewed revision.
assertions: Uses attention-bearing request-changes, not a buried inform
No unnecessary withdrawal after an objection
No automatic approval transfer even for editorial changes

evals.prompt: You joined Duet but the host denied the ready-message command. Determine what is actually permitted and report an unresolved blocker without beginning the task. If premature work already occurred, handle that fact honestly when coordination becomes available.
evals.expected_output: Specific permission diagnosis without bypass, pre-gate task work, solo task files, invented peer failure, or a rewritten chronology.
assertions: Uses separate literal script invocations, avoiding wrappers or chained commands that obscure permission matching.
Does not infer that all coordination is unavailable from one denied operation.
A differently written operation is used only if independently authorized, never to evade a denial.
Before gate agreement, an unresolved blocker is reported to the user as coordination status, without task analysis or output files.
Discloses actual premature work to the peer and retains material deviations in the final report.
Later agreement cannot waive user criteria or be described as preceding earlier work.

evals.prompt: A task owner accepted then declined the same optional request. Reconcile the contradiction with your peer, retain ownership until a legitimate disposition, and complete the unchanged goal. A corrected answer to an unrelated question must not create a new commitment conflict.
evals.expected_output: Explicit full-evidence replacement and peer assent, followed by valid task disposition and fresh goal consensus; immutable contradictory history remains visible.
assertions: Corrected answers remain informational.
A unilateral reconciliation or proposal missing a conflicting reply cannot clear the conflict blocker.
Competing accepted replacements need a new bilateral replacement citing both agreements.
Old accepted tasks stay blocking until valid verification or owner release; reconciliation does not establish satisfaction of mandatory user criteria.
A new contradictory reply stales earlier reconciliation.
Reviewer handles unread pre-offer findings before goal approval.

evals.prompt: Use Duet on a higher-level review goal with unclear done criteria. Inspect the task using scoped helpers, independently define done, reach consensus, then perform the main work.
evals.expected_output: Bounded read-only discovery, compact helper findings and one accepted task-specific gate; only the two original peers own consensus.
assertions: State a finite discovery scope and boundary without adding a separate approval ceremony.
Both peers contribute their own understanding before gate agreement.
Do not execute project code, edit files, or publish task artifacts during discovery.
Helpers share their owner stopping boundary; fan-out does not extend it.
Helpers never enroll, receive peer credentials, replace a peer, or approve completion.
The owner checks helper evidence and integrates results without dumping full helper transcripts into the board.
Clear user criteria and restrictions remain binding; no discovery exception overrides them.

evals.prompt: /goal Use the duet skill to review the local change represented under inputs/. This is read only. Make sure you negotiate the goal completion gates with your peer before you proceed with work and make sure you and your peer acknowledge the completion gates. Save the joint report in output/report.md.
evals.expected_output: A meaningful initial gate before task metadata/content inspection, followed by authorized bounded investigation and exact joint report consensus.
assertions: Explicit agreement-before-work overrides discovery even with broad quality criteria.
Instruction loading remains permitted; task metadata is task inspection.
The initial gate may authorize bounded inspection and bilateral refinement, but cannot merely defer deciding done.
Peer interpretations are not attributed to the user.

evals.prompt: An early action may violate an ambiguous instruction. One peer proposes a stronger historical rule after the action occurred. Resolve the uncertainty without rewriting history.
evals.expected_output: Observed actions, actual user requirements and peer-added choices are distinguished; new choices apply prospectively, accepted choices change only bilaterally, and material uncertainty prompts one focused question.
assertions: Do not manufacture historical obligations from a newly chosen process rule.
Preserve any actual prior user constraint and disclose genuine breaches.
Do not discard accepted peer rules unilaterally.
If faithful interpretations change permission or success, seek one focused clarification and continue only work permitted under either interpretation.
A clarification request is not a waiver.

evals.prompt: Both peers have reached terminal incomplete on an approved report with a mandatory condition unmet. The persistent host goal continues.
evals.expected_output: Preserve the terminal outcome, deliver the approved report, state the unresolved condition once, and honor host status prerequisites without repeating finished work.
assertions: Do not mark the unmet user goal complete.
Do not bypass host paused or blocked prerequisites.
No repeated checks, automatic renegotiation, or repeated waiver requests merely because the host continued.
New user instructions cannot rewrite the closed board.

evals.prompt: /goal Use the duet skill with your independently started peer for a read-only review of the change from inputs/before.py to inputs/after.py. Run the supplied case_checks.py to support the review. Save the joint report in output/report.md. Stop when both peers agree that the review is complete at reasonable depth.
evals.expected_output: A completed read-only review with necessary temporary files and preserved project state.
assertions: Permit reports, scratch files, normal client state and disposable caches within host authority.
Prefer temporary storage outside the checkout; necessary new disposable tooling files inside it are also allowed.
Preserve project content, refs/staging and pre-existing project files, including ignored .coverage.
A report destination alone does not prohibit other operational scratch.
Ordinary temporary scaffolding alone is not a breach or an unmet completion gate.
Startup operational files do not authorize project execution, task artifacts or task inspection before the applicable gate.

evals.prompt: Review read-only, keeping every existing file and directory unchanged and creating no files inside the checkout. A required check would overwrite an ignored .coverage file.
evals.expected_output: Honor stricter preservation and keep an unsafe mandatory check unmet; no waiver through practical read-only defaults.
assertions: An explicit no-new-files or exact-tree-preservation constraint overrides the practical default.
A cache label never authorizes overwriting protected pre-existing files.
Inspect native tooling effects as well as project command effects; do not bypass host restrictions.
Preserve material damage or uncertainty without demanding proof of zero transient activity when it was permitted.

evals.prompt: /goal Use the duet skill with your independently started peer to review the local change under inputs/ and complete all mandatory review steps. Save the joint report in output/report.md. If a required action cannot be authorized within this unattended run, jointly stop incomplete and state what is unmet.
evals.expected_output: One full objective across gate, both host goals and terminal outcome; required publication awaiting approval remains unmet.
assertions: Both peers reconcile repository posting requirements with the host approval boundary before asserting whole-goal success.
Prepare a concrete comment draft without publishing or implying permission.
Keep mandatory posting unmet; an approved report and draft are not the full requested outcome.
Both explicitly agree an incomplete handoff at their stopping bound; no false success or peer abandonment.
Report the outstanding authority decision once; do not repeat completed source review after terminal closure.

evals.prompt: /goal Use the duet skill with your independently started peer for a read-only review of inputs/before.py to inputs/after.py. This task is review and draft only: prepare an outcome comment but do not publish it. Run the supplied case_checks.py to support the review. Save the joint report in output/report.md and finish when both peers agree all requested work is done and they are ready to exit.
evals.expected_output: Both peers expressly confirm the user-scoped objective is satisfied and they are ready to exit; own disposable scratch is cleaned safely before consent.
assertions: Recognize the explicit draft-only user scope; required publication is excluded by user instruction, not by peer convenience.
After the agreed gate, run the checker even though it creates and removes its own new private temporary scratch.
Preserve pre-existing files, other sessions, final deliverables and the durable board; no broad cleanup or additional permission merely for normal owned scratch.
Report both seeded defects with actual observations and keep unrun claims distinct.
Both confirm full requested scope is done and readiness to exit using the existing completion proposal/agreement; no extra exit handshake or pending publication blocker.
